key_insight: UniMotion is the first single architecture that jointly understands and generates human motion, natural language, and RGB images by replacing discrete motion tokenization with a continuous, temporally-aware representation, preserving motion smoothness and cross-modal consistency.
problem_solved: Existing multimodal models handle only limited modality pairs (e.g., Motion–Text or Pose–Image) and rely on discrete tokenization that induces quantization errors and breaks temporal continuity; UniMotion unifies three modalities and avoids these drawbacks.
method: Unified single architecture that links motion, text, and images through a shared cross-modal latent space while keeping modality-specific encoders/decoders.
Continuous, temporally-aware motion representation (instead of discrete tokens) to preserve smooth dynamics and avoid quantization artifacts.

Joint training with cross-modal alignment and generative objectives so the model can perform both understanding (e.g., captioning, retrieval) and generation (e.g., text→motion, image-conditioned motion).
impact: Enables seamless tri-modal applications (text-driven animation, image-to-motion, motion captioning) with improved temporal fidelity and fewer artifacts; simplifies pipelines by consolidating tasks into one model for research and production use.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing a shared latent space with modality-specific encoders/decoders and cross-modal attention paths.
Before/after comparison: discrete-tokenized motion (choppy) vs UniMotion continuous motion (smooth) with skeleton animations.
Example multi-task panel: text→motion, image-conditioned motion, motion captioning outputs side-by-side.
Bar chart or table summarizing improvements in temporal continuity and cross-modal retrieval/generation metrics versus baselines.
paper_title: UniMotion: A Unified Framework for Motion-Text-Vision Understanding and Generation
paper_authors: Ziyi Wang, Xinshun Wang, Shuang Chen, Yang Cong, Mengyuan Liu
